image_description: A group of Australian Pelicans standing on a sandy shore next to blue water. The birds feature white plumage with black flight feathers, long pinkish bills with prominent gular pouches, and short legs. One pelican in the center stands tall, while others are seated or partially cropped at the edges.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Enormous bill with distensible gular pouch extending from lower mandible.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The central standing pelican and the seated pelican to its right clearly display the characteristic long bill with a visible, sagging gular pouch structure underneath.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Bill is enormous and elongated, vastly exceeding head length, with bright orange, yellow, or pink coloration during breeding.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bills are distinctly pinkish-flesh colored and significantly longer than the cranial portion of the head, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is large with prominent pouch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head-to-body ratio and the visible throat pouch are consistent with pelican anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Plumage is predominantly white, grey, or brown depending on species and season.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body exhibits heavy barrel-shaped torso of very large proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The seated birds show a bulky, rounded torso shape typical of the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings are extremely broad and long with dark flight feathers contrasting lighter body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct black primary/secondary flight feathers are clearly visible against the white body on multiple subjects.

The central standing pelican displays a distinct long neck with a natural curvature.
The rear profile of the seated birds shows a short tail structure consistent with the wedge shape description.
